text.p: PRAVDA - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik considers the expected current account deficit of around 45 billion crowns, or 7.7 percent of GDP, as "extremely high", and said that from the long-term perspective he saw the deficit at around three to four percent of GDP.
- Kozlik said he would prefer measures by the central bank that would reduce domestic consumption-oriented imports, but would not limit investment activities.

NARODNA OBRODA - Milan Cic, chairman of the Constitutional Court, said he had recevied several death threats in the past few weeks. The independent Association of Slovak Judges said the threats were politicaly motivated. The Constitutional Court has several times ruled against the ruling coalition.
- The government holds its regular sesison on Tuesday. The preliminary agenda does not include any major economic items.

- Heavy engineering company and former major Czechoslovak arms producer ZTS Martin, said its debts now totalled some seven billion crowns. ZTS said it would have to lay off some 800 employees next year.

- The Slovak Medical Chamber (SLK) and the medical trade union (LOZ) oppose the 1997 state budget on the grounds that it will not help stabilise the current bad situation in the country's health care sector.
- LOZ and SLK said they would call for protest strikes if the government does not adopt a strategy to prevent the imminent collapse in the health care sector.
SME - Some 55 deputies of the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) signed a pact with their party according to which they must hand back their mandate if they quit the party.
- Frantisek Gaulider, a former HZDS deputy whose mandate was withdrawn on the grounds of a treaty with the party after he had quit its club, said he would take the case to the Constitutional Court.
- One Chinese national was shot dead and several were injured in a gunfight at the Bratislava airport on Sunday.

- Some 55 percent Slovaks think government policy is not leading towards integration in the European Union and NATO, while about 26 percent think it is, according to a public opinion poll by the independent Focus agency.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The agriculture sector took loans worth 14.1 billion crowns last year with an average interest rate of 16 percent.
